summary: Frontend-only test of the festive Free World map (/world) at 390x800 and 1920x800 as super admin. The main fix works: elementFromPoint at the current node and at the yellow PLAY span hits the node/PLAY span, never the Santa canvas, in idle, win, try, ride and dance modes. Tapping the node or PLAY opens the level screen on the first tap (430-900ms) on mobile and desktop. Santa intro: shown once, Skip closes it, does not come back after a reload in the same tab. Demo flow works (PLAY DEMO, solved, REPLAY DEMO goes back to demo in about 700ms, Skip practice, START ATTEMPT). Three real official attempts were played and passed (L43 memory_match, L44 math_sprint, L45 simon_says). On the result screen, PLAY AGAIN goes back to the ready screen on one tap (about 1.2s, no extra API calls). RETURN TO WORLD closes on one tap (about 890ms). onFinished fires once, Santa enters 'win' mode with 'Ho Ho Ho! Level done!', and PLAY on the next node works during the celebration. Ride via CustomEvent shows the sleigh, 2 reindeer and snow trail with no console or WebGL errors (8 ride/win cycles: still 1 canvas, no context warnings). 'try' mode works. Replay of completed nodes could not be tested: the current GC has replay disabled, completed nodes show no 'REPLAY · FREE' and tapping L42 does nothing (by design). Two real problems found: (1) Performance. Festive map runs at about 18 fps on desktop vs 51 fps with the Original theme (relative drop about 65%; mobile about 20 fps). During a sleigh ride it drops further to about 11 fps, with a 470-580ms worst frame. (2) On mobile the level screen's close X (.fwv3-close, top 8-46px) is under the sticky site header (bottom 99px). Tapping X opens the hamburger menu instead of closing the game.

ui_bugs.issue: Close X (.fwv3-close, aria-label='Close') is at y=8-46px but the sticky site-header covers y=0-99px. elementFromPoint at the X returns data-testid='mobile-menu-toggle', so tapping X opens the mobile hamburger menu instead of closing the game. On desktop X works. The user's 'back doesn't work properly' complaint is likely this. Root cause: world.css:4782 'body:has(.fwv3-overlay) .fwv3-overlay { top:0 !important }' on mobile puts the card under the header. The z-index 10050 does not win, likely because the overlay sits in a lower stacking context than header z-40.

integration_issues.flow: Map performance with festive theme (the 'some lag' complaint)
integration_issues.issue: rAF fps (headless, compare relative values): festive about 18 fps vs Original 51 fps on desktop 1920x800, festive about 19-22 fps on mobile. During a sleigh ride about 11-12 fps with a 470-580ms worst frame. Experiment: turning off all CSS animations raised fps 18.6 to 25.3 (144 .pl-snow + 24 .pl-firework animations are running because FestiveFx renders for every section <=10, not only visible ones). Hiding .pl-santa with display:none did NOT raise fps, so the r3f Canvas keeps rendering every frame even when hidden. Santa3D also switches the Canvas key 'ride'/'stand', which destroys and recreates the WebGL context on every ride start and end; that causes the long frame.

design_issues.screen: Level entry screen stat cards (mobile and desktop)
issues: A vertical purple dashed line runs through the middle 'GAME' stat card over the game name text (e.g. 'Memory Match (pairs)', 'Sudoku Mini (4x4)'). It looks like a decorative element leaking behind or through the card.
'CORRECT 20 / 20' is shown for Memory Match (7 pairs) and for Math Sprint with wrong answers. The value looks hard-coded or wrong for client games.

action_items: Mobile: make .fwv3-close reachable. Either keep the overlay below the header (top: var(--pl-topbar-h)), or raise the overlay above the header / give the close button a top offset clearing the header. Check that elementFromPoint at the X returns the X.

Santa3D: avoid remounting the Canvas on ride/stand (drop key={riding?'ride':'stand'}; keep one Canvas and move the camera/scene instead). Use frameloop='demand' or pause rendering when the avatar is off-screen or hidden (IntersectionObserver + invalidate), and do not mount SantaAvatar/Santa3D at all when mapTheme.theme !== 'festive' (today it is only display:none).
SantaAvatar: the pl-santa-celebrate handler plays jingles and voice even when the map theme is Original (Santa is hidden but audio still plays on win/try/ride). Gate it on festive theme.
FestiveFx: render snow/fireworks only for the section(s) in the viewport, or one fixed overlay (now 144 snow + 24 firework animations run together). Consider prefers-reduced-motion.
Reduce SnowTrail cost during ride (3 trails, 240 points updated every frame on the CPU plus a material opacity change) or lower counts on mobile.
Fix the 'CORRECT 20/20' result stat for client skill games.
critical_code_review_comments: Santa3D.jsx: <Canvas key={riding ? 'ride' : 'stand'}> creates a new WebGL context on every ride start/end. This gives a 470-580ms jank frame at the exact moment the user returns to the map and may try to tap PLAY.
Santa3D.jsx: the default frameloop='always' renders at full rate even when the parent is display:none (classic theme, or the avatar scrolled off-screen).

SantaAvatar.jsx: the position-change effect triggers ride(), and that clears the 'win' celebration timers. After a passed level, 'Ho Ho Ho! Level done!' is replaced by the ride about 1s later, once the progress refresh moves the avatar. This is fine, but the 'win' mode is short-lived.

PrizeLeagueWorld onFinished is only called from the result screen's CONTINUE/RETURN TO WORLD. After PLAY AGAIN followed by close X / Back, the map progress is not refreshed and no celebration is shown.
WorldCanvas.jsx is 3800+ lines and FreeWorldNumberSequenceV3.jsx is 2800 lines. Both should be split.

Console: repeated 'GL Driver Message ... GPU stall due to ReadPixels' warnings (headless software GL, low priority). Admin page logs a 'cannot be a child of <option>' hydration warning (<span> inside <option>) in AdminLayout.

rca of the issue: User report 'play/replay doesn't work properly, some lag'. (a) Click interception by the Santa canvas is FIXED: CSS .pl-santa * pointer-events:none and canvas style pointerEvents none were verified with elementFromPoint in all Santa modes. (b) Lag: the festive theme costs about 65% of frame rate vs Original. The causes are 168 CSS snow/firework animations in off-screen sections, an always-rendering r3f Canvas, and a WebGL context recreated on every ride (key switch) with 240 CPU-updated particles. The worst frames of about 0.5s happen right after a level when the sleigh ride starts. This makes taps feel unresponsive, but they do register. (c) 'Back doesn't work' on mobile: the close X of the level screen is under the sticky header, so the tap opens the hamburger menu. Repro: 390x800, /world, tap PLAY, tap X at top-right, and the mobile menu opens.
